response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Oh, I'm just a nobody. You'll probably run into a good handful of Eremite mercenaries like me on just a short trip to pick a Sumeru Rose outside the city.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Haniyyah probably doesn't remember me either. Although she did help someone as insignificant as me back then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Do you know Haniyyah as well?

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Technically, I know her, but she doesn't know me. She saved my life before, and I haven't been able to repay her for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Haniyyah said that she's just an ordinary beast tamer. Could it be that she's actually really strong?

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Well, it was indeed her remarkable beast-taming abilities that saved my life.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Back then, I was in charge of receiving Sumpter Beasts that belonged to enemies. The Sumpter Beasts were submissive only to their original owners and nearly crushed every bone in my body.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Thank goodness Haniyyah was there when it happened. She used a special technique to calm the enraged Sumpter Beasts before they sent me to the afterlife. Haniyyah said she was just doing her job, and she even refused my thank-you gift.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... Paimon never would've expected something like that to happen...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That was very kind of her!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Yeah, on top of that, some Sumpter Beasts were once bewitched by the hilichurls and became extremely hostile toward humans. Sumpter Beasts can also become enraged if their feed is laced with suspicious mushrooms.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Haniyyah's our only hope whenever something like that happens. She seems to always befriend the Sumpter Beasts, turning them into gentle giants after just a half day of training.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who would've thought that the work Haniyyah only briefly mentioned had such a great impact! She really is amazing!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Gentle Sumpter Beasts are worth quite a bit, whether you're selling to the Eremites or ordinary merchants. However, Haniyyah's fees remain extremely cheap.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: She seems to really enjoy communicating with animals, and her passion for beast taming is far greater than any desire to make money. And... that's exactly why I have no idea how to repay her...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're curious too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Haniyyah's also helped us in the past. We want to do something for her in return too!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Ha! Well then, let's work together and see if we can get to know our beast-taming friend a little better!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: However, it's been a while since I've seen Haniyyah. She seems to have changed... I wonder if she's still as approachable as before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, did something upset you? Don't worry. Bad things will pass and your time will eventually come!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Wow, I would've never thought that someone like me would be able to attract the attention of renowned individuals like you guys.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: I'm not sad, I'm just reflecting on some things, that's all. Maybe it isn't such a bad thing, after all...

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: I suppose it would be beneficial for Haniyyah's career if she were to be a little more insistent at times.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haniyyah? Be more insistent?

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Long story short, as a talented beast tamer, sometimes she needs to command a certain level of "respect" to prevent people from trying to scam her.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Haniyyah used to be an energetic and happy person. She wore her heart on her sleeve, and she never had the slightest intention of hiding her emotions. I often worry if someone with ill intent will take advantage of her.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: But looking at how she is now, she must've experienced something that changed her. Her thoughts aren't on display anymore. It puts my mind at ease.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't really understand... But Paimon kinda knows what you're saying.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: My apologies for blabbering to myself. Just... see it as a useless guy worrying about a young girl he's indebted to.

choices.text: Are you a competitor as well?

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: No, but you can think of me as a spectator with a stake in the competition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A stake in the competition? That sounds serious!

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: It is, actually. I may lose my job over this competition.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: You may have already heard about that Kautilya guy. He wants to use trained Fungi to replace some of the mercenaries in protecting important areas or performing dangerous tasks.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: However, the situations that mercenaries face are often complex. They require a large amount of experience and split-second decision-making to get the job done. It's not so much whether the Fungi can fulfill the task or not — it's the possibility that the Fungi might be taken advantage of by criminals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? We've never heard of that before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But no one in their right mind would send their Fungi companions into combat with other monsters, right? What is that Kautilya guy thinking...?

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: I would have been able to casually enjoy the show if I hadn't heard that.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: Hopefully, the wealthy merchant that sponsored the competition has a good head on his shoulders. There's a domineering quality to his movements. It's safe to assume he's been through quite a bit as well.

response.speaker: Thabit
response.text: He should know that people are always more reliable than trained beasts or monsters during critical moments.
